chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him:

May I perform ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and other reasons in the latrine in which urination takes place, while I am wearing Sindhī sandals, so I perform ghusl while the sandals remain on me as they are?
He said: "If the water that flows from your body reaches the bottoms of your feet, then do not wash the bottoms of your feet."

key_terms.أَسْفَلَ قَدَمَيْكَ: the bottoms or soles of your feet
key_terms.الْكَنِيفِ: a privy or latrine used as a place of relieving oneself
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the water used in the ritual bath
key_terms.جَسَدِكَ: your body, from which the water flows during ghusl
key_terms.نَعْلٌ سِنْدِيَّةٌ: Sindhī sandals worn on the feet

ai.seo_question: Does water flowing during ghusl count for washing the soles of the feet?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing ghusl (ritual bath) in a place used for urination while wearing sandals. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that if the water flowing from the body reaches the soles of the feet, then there is no need to wash the soles separately.
